To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cytoprotective activity of SNO-HSAs is enhanced by binding of oleate and that this effect is due to increased S-transnitrosylation of glutathione and of albumin.
the binding of oleate to human serum albumin increases its S-nitrosation by liver cells, and that the binding of fatty acids to S-nitrosoalbumin increases its cytoprotectivity.
the binding of fatty acids to S-nitrosothiols, such as S-nitroserine or S-nitroalbumin, enhances their nitric oxide (NO)-mediated biological activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new mechanism for cytoprotection by SNO-HSA.
the mechanism of the cytoprotective activity of SNO-HAS.
the role of fatty acids as modulators of S-nitrosylation and denitrosylation in the liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
S-transnitrosylation by fatty acid-bound SNO-HSA is enhanced by fatty acid binding.
SNO-HSA is a novel type of nitric oxide donor and that its nitric oxide release is facilitated by fatty acids.
S-nitrosylation of albumin, which occurs at a rate of about 1 mol of nitric oxide per 100 mol of albumin per minute, can protect cells from apoptosis and from the toxic effect of nitric oxide.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SNO-HSA is a novel type of nitric oxide donor that is activated by fatty acid binding.
fatty acids enhance S-transnitrosating activity in cells by increasing the affinity of SNO-HSAs for cell membranes and by enhancing SNO-HSA-mediated nitric oxide delivery.
fatty acid binding to the S-nitrosated albumin molecule increases its binding to the hepatocyte cell membrane and enhances its S-transnitrosating activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fatty acid binding to albumin enhances its cytoprotection.
the cytoprotective activity of SNO-HS is enhanced by binding of fatty acids.

the binding of oleate to albumin enhances its S-nitrosothiol-mediated cytoprotective activity by facilitating the transfer of nitric oxide to the cell surface and by increasing the rate of S-transnitrosylation.
